paragraphs: Rabbi Abba bar Natan (see Rava bar Natan). A man lost his tefillin during the festival’s intermediate days. He came before Rabbi Chananel, who sent him to Rabbi Abba b.N. and told him, “Give him your tefillin and go write some for yourself.” Rav told him, “Go write for him.” Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Ellu Megallechin, halakhah 4. (Semag, positive commandments, Laws of Tefillin, commandment 22, reads: Rav Chananel sent to Rabbah bar bar Chana and told the scribe, “Go give him your tefillin.”) It appears that he wrote tefillin. Rav Assi thought he was mocking him, grew angry with him, and he died, Jerusalem Talmud, Nazir, chapter Kohen Gadol (7), halakhah 2. The rabbis of Caesarea; Rabbi Chiyya bar Vava in his name, Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Hacholetz. Perhaps Issi was his brother. There is also Rav Natan bar Abba.
